paragraphs: FYLD sells a platform that turns the realities of frontline work into structured, real-time data. It is built for critical infrastructure operators who need jobs done right the first time. The pitch starts from lost time, with the company saying a fifth of a field worker's day goes to paper processes and unseen admin.

A phone app converts video, photo, audio and text into work assessments. Crews use it to record progress through the day, evidence issues and flag problems to managers. On the office side, the cloud product alerts managers only to events that need action. Centralised records leave an audit trail the company positions as protection against fines.

The company reports injuries and incidents falling 20 percent for one client over a twelve-month period. It also claims at least six times return on investment across sectors. FYLD announced a $41 million Series B round aimed at infrastructure field work. Amey has deployed the platform for highways operations, according to a company announcement.

quote.text: Records don’t improve performance. Intelligence does.
